school: Development Economics, Human Capital Theory, Agricultural Economics
legacy: Theodore Schultz helped transform economics by emphasizing the value of people as productive assets. His work encouraged economists to view education, skills, health and knowledge as investments capable of generating long-term economic growth and societal advancement.
earlyLife: Raised in a rural environment, Schultz developed firsthand familiarity with agriculture and the challenges faced by farming communities. These experiences shaped his interest in understanding economic development, productivity and the factors that influence prosperity within both rural and urban societies.
majorContributions: Schultz advanced the idea that investments in education, training, health and knowledge contribute significantly to economic growth. He also conducted influential research on agricultural productivity and economic development, highlighting the importance of human capabilities in improving living standards and creating opportunities for future prosperity.
laterLife: Throughout his later career, Schultz continued researching development, poverty reduction and the economic value of education. His work influenced policymakers, researchers and international organizations seeking sustainable approaches to economic advancement and human welfare.
whyImportant: Modern economics increasingly recognizes that human knowledge and skills are among society's most valuable resources. Theodore Schultz helped establish this perspective, influencing economic policy, education planning and development strategies around the world.
